what: Sheets, joint compound, tape and screws for a room
title: Drywall Calculator: How Many Sheets of Drywall Do I Need? | ProjectMath
description: Calculate drywall sheets (4x8, 4x10 or 4x12) for walls and ceiling, plus joint compound, tape, screws and corner bead. Free, with a printable shopping list.
lede: Enter the room size to see how many drywall sheets to buy, after doors and windows, plus joint compound, tape and screws. The example is a 14 by 12 foot room.

faq.q: How many sheets of drywall do I need for a 12x12 room?
faq.a: A 12 by 12 room with 8 foot walls has 384 sq ft of wall. Take off one door and one window (36 sq ft), add 10% waste, and you need about 12 sheets of 4 by 8 drywall for the walls, plus 5 more if you hang the ceiling.
Longer sheets cover more with fewer joints, so there is less taping. 4 by 8 sheets are lighter and easier to carry and hang alone. Many pros use 4 by 12 on long walls and ceilings.

faq.q: How much joint compound do I need?
faq.a: Rules of thumb range widely. This calculator uses about 9 gallons of ready-mixed compound per 1,000 sq ft for taping and two finish coats, which is about one 4.5 gallon bucket per 500 sq ft. Buy one extra if you are learning.

faq.q: How many screws per sheet of drywall?
faq.a: About 1 screw per square foot, so roughly 32 for a 4 by 8 sheet. Ceilings and local code may require closer spacing.

faq.q: What thickness of drywall should I use?
faq.a: 1/2 inch is standard for walls. Ceilings often use 1/2 inch sag-resistant or 5/8 inch board, and 5/8 inch Type X is used where fire-rated walls are required, such as between a garage and the house.
